parsed.explanation: A national bill criminalising identifying as transgender, crossdressing and promotion, with up to 3 years' imprisonment and a duty to report, passed in May 2026 and widely expected to receive assent, is a state-imposed tier-1 exposure if outed. Existing law retains up to 3 years for 'unnatural carnal knowledge', mob justice is documented, national security raided and closed LGBTQ premises in the capital, and there is no anti-discrimination recourse. No capital penalty or custody-abuse pattern is documented, and the bill was not yet assented, keeping the rating above the 0.15 anchors but below the 0.25 short-sentence anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, visa or screening rule documented; unresolved whether identification, crossdressing or duty-to-report offences apply to short-term visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch or presentation could trigger the national identification offence at any police or official encounter, but border practice is uncertain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2026 bill as reported: up to 3 years for identifying as transgender, longer for promotion/advocacy, plus duty to report prohibited acts; 2024 version similar.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Supreme Court dismissed challenges as premature and deferred review until assent.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A report, mob confrontation or official check could convert identification into investigation and custody; no visitor-specific immunity documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No national prison placement rule, trans unit, solitary practice, bathroom or ward rule documented in any source.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Placement is an open question, not a documented exposure; it cannot be assumed safe, and absence of a rule leaves discretion unregulated.

care_services.exposure: No visitor care-access, HRT-import or hospital-placement rule documented. Resident conversion therapy is abusive but is not a visitor service rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Bill criminalises identifying as transgender and crossdressing; passage attributed to religious-leader pressure; surveyed nationals largely opposed decriminalisation citing religion, culture and children; national security raided an LGBTQ office.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. President previously withheld assent in 2024, but has signalled willingness to sign and assent was widely expected in 2026.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing plus societal framing of LGBT people as a threat to children gives police and community actors license to report or confront.

minors_guardians.exposure: No rule documented for a trans minor visitor or for a guardian travelling with one; age-specific application of identification or crossdressing offences is not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. Resident family eviction and conversion-therapy practices do not establish a visitor-minor exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob justice against perceived LGBT people documented; LGBTQ centre forced to close and rights-group office raided and closed by national security in the capital in 2021; groups now operate secretly or online.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No anti-discrimination protection documented; a paralegal initiative for residents is documented but no visitor remedy or police protection outcome is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public hostility with state closure of venues leaves a visitor with no documented protective police response and heightened outing and confrontation risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; judicial review deferred until presidential assent; no enforcement record yet for the 2026 bill; entry, prison-placement and visitor-application questions unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Paralegal initiative documented for residents in court; no documented effective remedy for a detained or expelled visitor. Courts dismissed the 2024 challenges.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending assent and deferred review mean the protection question is temporal: exposure becomes statutory on assent, with no documented pre-assent remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that presentation/identity is criminalised and remedies are illusory, but here custody beatings, months-long arbitrary detention and a capital provision are not documented, so this case sits higher than 0.15.

Lower than 0.25-A: raids and fines with rare, brief imprisonment there, versus an explicit up to 3 years for identifying as transgender, a duty to report, and national-security closure of premises here.

Materially lower than 0.35-B: there detention is hours-long with fines and no imprisonment, whereas here the statute expressly authorises imprisonment for transgender identity itself and a reporting duty.

parsed.synthesis: The combined national regime is the operative exposure: a widely expected assent to a bill punishing transgender identification and crossdressing, layered on existing 3-year sexuality law, mob justice and security-service closures, with no anti-discrimination recourse and courts deferring review until assent. Unknown entry and prison-placement rules are not counted as safety. Absence of a documented capital penalty or custody-abuse campaign prevents a 0.15 rating, but statutory imprisonment for identity itself places the case at the severe/high-risk boundary at 0.20.
